facts.value: The channel selects the acquired CARDControl and SRAM flash ID. The new CARDID receives the requested encoding, card size, OS time, VI status, SRAM counter bias and language, and time-transformed flash-ID bytes; deviceID is set to zero. Two empty directory images and two zero-initialized FAT images are checksummed, with check codes 0 and 1 distinguishing each pair's copies. Card block count feeds the FAT free-block count as cBlock - CARD_NUM_SYSTEM_BLOCK, not the CARDID; the FAT last-slot field is CARD_NUM_SYSTEM_BLOCK - 1. DCStoreRange stores the prepared work area to memory before the asynchronous sequence. FormatCallback later consumes these retained images for system-block writes.
facts.rationale: Corrects the existing assignment of block count to CARDID and the misleading description of duplicate check codes while preserving the supported input sources and asynchronous work-area flow.

evidence.why: Shows each identity input, per-copy check codes, FAT geometry fields, checksum calls, cache-store call and initial dispatch.
Shows continuation writes consuming the prepared work-area images and successful final metadata copying.
